description: FS-GG typed coordination engine — the schedulability model behind `fsgg-coord` as one total function over a board-state snapshot, plus the typed IO layer that drives it. It IS the coordination tool (ADR-0034/ADR-0040): the `fsgg-coord` shim resolves and execs it; there is no bash left to shadow.
releaseNotes:
0.51.0 — a MINOR coherent-set cut. The review protocol now represents a case it previously refused.

`.github#2527`. A pull request whose head moves AFTER its review chain completed and was
host-accepted had no representation. The only honest response to a moved head — a full fresh
independent review of the tree that will actually merge — posts a second initial marker, and the
chain then failed closed with "the initial review marker is carried by 2 comments; exactly one is
required": a refusal that describes the symptom and names no remedy. Critic succession
(`.github#2417`) requires a STUCK round and the repair phase requires EXHAUSTION, so neither reached
a chain that had finished and was then invalidated by a push.

WHAT THIS CUT ADDS. `Driver.liveReviewComments` partitions a pull request's review comments, and
`Review` classifies the protocol state from the surviving set. A chain is retired when, and only
when, a host-acceptance marker names that chain's initial-review comment URL AND carries an
`accepted-head` other than the current head — both read from that marker's own already-required
fields. `Review.Verdict` carries the retired chains, and `review --json` reports them as
`retiredChains`.

WHY MINOR RATHER THAN PATCH. This is receiver-visible behaviour, not prose: a receiver running
`review` against unchanged comment evidence can now obtain a different action than it did before this
cut, the JSON contract gains a field, and Core's published signature surface gains the retirement
types that carry it.

WHAT STAYS REFUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT. Two competing initial markers with no intervening
accepted-then-moved head still fail closed. So does an acceptance whose `accepted-head` is the
current head, and one whose `initial-review` names no initial marker on the pull request. Retirement
is admitted only on what the acceptance marker's own required fields carry, rather than on a grant a
caller supplies, because the one-initial-marker rule is what stops a stranger silently continuing
another critic's chain. What is read is that marker's STRUCTURE, not the truth of its `accepted-head`:
a forged acceptance marker will retire a live chain. That confers strictly less than the forgery it
presupposes — a forged acceptance at the CURRENT head already yields an accepted chain outright, while
this route yields only one awaiting a fresh acceptance at the current head — and the value is published
in `retiredChains` where a reader can see it.
Retirement never edits, reorders or drops evidence at the source: a retired chain stays exactly as
its critic posted it.

ALSO RIDING THIS CUT. `.github#2525` landed engine changes before this branch and could not move the
coherent-set scalar itself, so its work is carried by this version rather than by one of its own. This
entry describes what `.github#2527` adds; it is NOT an inventory of the tagged tree, which is whatever
the tagged commit holds. `registry/CHANGELOG.md` and the tag range are the inventory.

Adopt 0.51.0.

0.50.7 — a PATCH-LINE cut with NO ENGINE SOURCE CHANGE, published so the
coordination kit can carry a corrected `pnext-item` skill body. The three packages resolve one scalar
(`FsggCoherentSetVersion`, `Directory.Build.props`) by construction, so a kit-only content fix moves this
package's version too. That is the coherent-set design (`.github#2402`), not an engine delta.

NO COMPILED ENGINE SOURCE MOVED SINCE 0.50.6, and this claim is measured rather than copied from the
entry below. `git diff --name-only` over `src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli`, `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core` and
`src/FS.GG.Coord.GitHub`, between the `kit/v0.50.6` tag commit and the commit these notes ship at, names
exactly ONE path: `src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli/FS.GG.Coord.Cli.fsproj` — this project file, carrying this very
property. No `.fs` file differs. The only other change in the cut is the coherent-set scalar in
`Directory.Build.props`, which is outside those three trees.

Stated that way deliberately. An earlier draft of this paragraph said the diff "is EMPTY", which was
true when it was measured — one commit before these notes existed — and false the moment the sentence
was written into the file it was describing. A release note is read at the version it ships with, so an
evidence claim in one must hold AT that commit, not at the commit it was taken on.

WHY IT COULD NOT RIDE 0.50.6 (`.github#2526`). Three places in this repository stated as current fact
that `claim-generation` is advisory-only "until this job is genuinely armed into branch protection". It
has been a REQUIRED status context on `main` since `.github#1858`, and `.github#2517` replaced
`Landable.fs`'s hand-written `advisoryCheckNames` literal with the derived COMPLEMENT of the base
branch's required contexts, so the engine's own rollup scores it `Blocking` as well. Those three prose
claims were the last copies of the old answer, and one of them is packed into the kit as
`pnext-item/SKILL.md`. No behaviour changed: no gate, workflow trigger, or engine path was edited.

`kit-auto-publish` tags on merge to `main`, so `FS.GG.Kit 0.50.6` was cut and published from
`.github#2512`'s merge commit minutes before this branch merged `origin/main`. The published 0.50.6 is
byte-faithful to its tagged tree — the pack was correct — but that tree predates this fix, and its
`SKILL.md` still contains "stays advisory in the engine's own rollup". Tags are immutable, so the
corrected body cannot reach receivers under 0.50.6. This cut is how it does.

0.50.6 — a PATCH-LINE cut that COMPLETES a coherent set that 0.50.5 could not
complete, and that carries the engine changes which landed between 0.50.4 and the commit it is tagged at.

DO NOT ADOPT 0.50.5. It is a permanent two-of-three set. `FS.GG.Kit 0.50.5` and `FS.GG.Drivers 0.50.5`
published to both feeds; this package's publish was then REFUSED by `check-engine-release-notes`
(`.github#1762`) because this very property still began with `0.50.4` while `Version` had moved to
`0.50.5`. Correcting that needs a new commit, and `.github#1772`'s sibling-tag precondition requires
all three tags to name the SAME commit, so 0.50.5 could not be finished from a corrected tree —
re-cutting it is the re-pack divergence `.github#2240` documents. This is the same shape 0.50.1 had,
and it is recorded the same way in `registry/dependencies.yml`. Adopt 0.50.6.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED (`.github#2512`). `check-engine-release-notes` had a PR-time arm already, but
its workflow `paths:` filter selected only this project file — not `Directory.Build.props`, where
`FsggCoherentSetVersion` (and therefore this package's `Version`) is declared. PR #2507 bumped the
scalar there and touched nothing else that filter selected, so the gate never ran on the PR that
created the mismatch and first spoke at release time, after two packages had shipped irrevocably.
That filter and the checker's own `PATHS_SUBJECT` now both name `Directory.Build.props`; the checker
additionally refuses a `Version` that does not resolve from `FsggCoherentSetVersion`, so a version it
cannot trace to the coherent-set scalar is no longer something it will bless.

THE ENGINE SOURCE IS *NOT* BYTE-IDENTICAL TO 0.50.4. `.github#2324` is among the changes it carries.

THESE NOTES DO NOT ENUMERATE THE REST, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE — DO NOT "FIX" IT BY ADDING A LIST.
Earlier drafts of this entry tried three times to state the engine delta exactly, and each attempt was
wrong in a new way: one copied the "byte-identical to 0.50.4" line from the entry below, after a commit
had already landed underneath it; one added a corroborating aside about neighbouring entries which
itself endorsed a false claim; one gave an exhaustive count, and a later merge to `main` falsified it
almost immediately.

THE COMMON FAULT WAS NOT CARELESSNESS, IT WAS ADDRESS. A release note is written before the commit it
ships from exists — the tag lands on a MERGE commit, and `main` keeps moving until it does. So an
exhaustive claim about the tagged tree is not merely hard to get right here, it is not answerable from
here at all, and the sibling-tag precondition (`.github#1772`) forbids the follow-up commit that would
correct it. The remedy is to stop asserting it, not to assert it more carefully.

FOR THE AUTHORITATIVE LIST, ASK THE TAGGED TREE. `python3 scripts/check-engine-freshness.py` enumerates
the engine commits since `coord-engine/v0.50.4`, and this coherent set's row in
`registry/dependencies.yml` records the range with its evidence. `.github#2512`'s post-merge release
obligation re-runs that enumeration against the actual merge commit immediately before tagging, so the
record is made where the evidence exists rather than guessed here.

PATCH-LINE, AND CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
`git diff coord-engine/v0.50.4..coord-engine/v0.50.6 -- src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is this repo's
standing test — no verb, flag, help entry, render name, result name or exit code may move. That command
is run against the merge commit before the tag is cut, and a non-empty result means this cut is not a
patch and these notes are wrong.

0.50.4 — no engine behavior change. `.github#2496` edited kit-packed content
(`pnext-item/SKILL.md`) after `FS.GG.Kit 0.50.3` had already been packed at `42c63af9`, so
`check-kit-published-coherence` reds on `main`: the published 0.50.3 kit manifest differs from
canonical on that one file. This bump exists to let the coherent set republish with current canonical
content, not to announce a new engine fix; the engine source under `src/FS.GG.Coord.*` is
byte-identical to 0.50.3. See 0.50.3's own notes below for the prior release's substantive changes.

0.50.3 — no engine behavior change. `.github#2471` edited kit-packed content
(the `pnext-item` skill and the `stale_guard` shell module) after 0.50.2 had already published, so
`check-kit-published-coherence`'s PR arm required this coherent-set scalar to advance again before that
PR could land (0.50.2 is not STRICTLY GREATER than the already-published 0.50.2). This bump exists to
satisfy that gate, not to announce a new engine fix; the engine source under `src/FS.GG.Coord.*` is
byte-identical to 0.50.2. See 0.50.2's own notes below for the substantive engine changes.

0.50.2 — the completed coherent-set cut. FOUR DEFECT-CLASS ENGINE FIXES
plus two hardening changes, and the first version at which FS.GG.Kit, FS.GG.Drivers and this engine
are all three published together since 0.50.0 (.github#2381).

WHY 0.50.2 AND NOT 0.50.1. The 0.50.1 cut published FS.GG.Kit and FS.GG.Drivers to both feeds and
then REFUSED to publish this engine: `check-engine-release-notes` (.github#1762) correctly red-flagged
that this property still began with `0.50.0`, so the package listing would have announced another
release's notes. Both sibling packages were already immutable at 0.50.1 and the coherent-set gate
requires all three tags to name the SAME commit, so 0.50.1 could not be completed from a corrected
tree — it stands as a permanent two-of-three set. 0.50.2 is the whole set, cut from one commit with
this property corrected first. FS.GG.Kit 0.50.1 and FS.GG.Drivers 0.50.1 should not be adopted on
their own; adopt 0.50.2.

WHAT SHIPS SINCE 0.50.0 (defect-class marked DEFECT):

DEFECT  landable now attributes run gating to bad/pending check-runs rather than suite membership
        (.github#2454). Before this, a merge gate could red on a check merely BELONGING to a suite
        rather than on that check having failed.
DEFECT  the markerless-row PR probe widened to `In review`, not just `Ready`/`Backlog`
        (.github#2384) — the projection oscillation that made an unclaimed in-review row flip
        columns between reads.
DEFECT  `done`'s .github#2427 passed-over-foreign-closer advisory now goes to stderr rather than
        stdout and the durable receipt (.github#2444), restoring stdout purity for callers that
        parse it.
DEFECT  critic-succession's "exact critic" guard no longer accepts a generic agent-type string as
        proof of "the same critic" (.github#2451) — it bound to a review-marker field that is not
        always a minted identity, weakening the independent-review contract itself.
        `isGenericCriticIdentity` is kept private to Driver.fs/Review.fs.
        the #353 collision scan now runs on `claim`, warning by default and refusing with
        `--refuse-overlap` (.github#2459) — `claim` previously bypassed the overlap check entirely,
        so two workers could hold intersecting touch-sets.
        the accepted fsgg-sdd validator `toolVersion` is now an explicit vetted set rather than a
        bare literal (.github#2465), with an error naming the reported version and the accepted set.
        Previously ANY FS.GG.SDD.Cli release — patch included — broke `cycle advance` until someone
        edited F# source.

NO WIRE-SURFACE CHANGE. `git diff coord-engine/v0.50.0..HEAD -- src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is
empty across all of the above: no verb, flag, help entry, render name, result name or exit code is
added, removed or re-spelled. This is a patch-line cut.

PRIOR 0.50.0.

0.50.0 — VERSIONING-SCHEME CHANGE, NOT A BEHAVIOR CUT (.github#2402):

FS.GG.Coord.Cli's `<Version>` is no longer this project's own independent literal. FS.GG.Kit,
FS.GG.Drivers and this engine are now released from one shared MSBuild property
(0.51.0, Directory.Build.props), so a bump to any one of the three moves all
three together and the three cannot diverge from each other the way FS.GG.Kit 0.49.0 and
FS.GG.Drivers 0.18.0 diverged from this engine's 0.23.0 twenty minutes apart on 2026-08-10
(commits f26da6ed/d48e1ec2). The set starts one MINOR above 0.49.0 — FS.GG.Kit's version at the
time the set was declared, the highest of the three prior independent versions — rather than at
0.49.0 itself, because 0.49.0 was already the newest FS.GG.Kit published on nuget.org and any PR
editing FS.GG.Kit.csproj (which adopting this property does) must declare a version strictly
greater than what is already published. Either way no member appears to downgrade (see
docs/registry/compatibility.md for the full migration note).

THIS IS NOT THE USUAL PATCH/MINOR CLASSIFICATION. `git diff coord-engine/v0.23.0..HEAD --
src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli/Options.fs` is empty: no verb, flag, help
entry, render name, result name or exit code is added, removed or re-spelled by this cut, which
under this repository's usual 0.x rule would make it a PATCH. The jump from 0.23.0 to 0.50.0 is
instead dictated entirely by the coherent-set adoption above, stated here rather than left to look
like an unexplained large PATCH-shaped bump.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.23.0):

0.23.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line: `driver --events [--cursor FILE]` (.github#2135,
PR #2327) derives material transitions and the complete active-item inventory from live board/claim/
PR/review/delivery facts, with an optional durable idempotency cursor file — a caller-visible flag,
help entry, and render mode `driver` did not have before. Two repair rounds close #2135's residue:
persistent-Unreadable silence, corrupt-cursor collapse and CLI coverage (round 1); a directory at the
--cursor path is now refused rather than silently treated as absent (round 2).

This cut also ships #2264's lifecycle Status projection (PR #2271): board reconciliation now converges
the Project Status field from live PR/review/CI/delivery facts instead of relying on point-in-time
writes at claim/release time, with orphan-claim handling and a single reconciled status writer so two
passes cannot disagree.

TWO DEFECT-class fixes are included:

- #2306 (PR #2323) — a `widen`/`set-paths` call refused with `OVERLAP` no longer mutates the held
  item's touch-set declaration. Before this fix, the refused paths were written into the declaration
  anyway, so a caller who read the refusal as "nothing changed" held a wider, silently-drifted
  declaration than they asked for or than the refusal implied.
- #2245 acceptance 6 (PR #2326) — `RepoScope.resolve` now maps the rostered short id `sir` to
  `EHotwagner/S.I.R.`, closing the scheduling-namespace split where a receiver's board rows (Repo
  Scope `sir`) and the engine's own `--repo`/reservation keys (canonical `S.I.R.`) resolved to two
  different repositories: `batch --repo S.I.R.` and `batch --repo sir` could each admit candidates
  that overlapped the other's live reservations.

EIGHTEEN merged engine commits since 0.22.1. `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` (the exit-code wire
contract) is untouched by this cut — the MINOR classification is carried entirely by the new
`--events`/`--cursor` flag surface in `Options.fs`, consistent with this repository's 0.x policy that
new CLI vocabulary is the caller-observable-change signal whenever there is no Major line to take.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.22.1):

0.22.1 — PATCH: #2308 fixes empty claim-marker reads so an unreadable or empty
response refuses instead of inventing a safe-looking unclaimed state. The CLI verb, flag, result, and
exit-code vocabulary is unchanged; this is stable (no prerelease suffix).

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.22.0):

0.22.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line: explicit source-bound delivery-route receipts and
typed intake transactions add caller-visible command, result, and refusal vocabulary. This cut also ships
the #2300 scheduling and #2313 reconcile read-amplification defect fixes. The release is intentionally
minor because Protocol.fs changes make the new delivery-route gate and transaction surface observable to
every receiver; it remains stable (no prerelease suffix).

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.21.1):

0.21.1 — PATCH: a CLOSED but UNSTAMPED item is still in flight, and review-marker
recognition stops discarding the markers it cannot place (.github#2225, .github#2221).

FOUR merged engine commits since 0.21.0. The wire surface `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is
UNTOUCHED — and so is the CLI verb table, `src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli/Options.fs`. PATCH is MEASURED rather
than argued: `git diff coord-engine/v0.21.0..HEAD -- src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs
src/FS.GG.Coord.Cli/Options.fs` is empty, so no verb, flag, help entry, render name, result name or
exit code is added, removed or re-spelled. The four commits touch only `Client.fs`, `Snapshot.fs`,
`Driver.fs` and `Scan.fs`. This registry contract's declared surface names the CLI VERB surface
first and independently of the exit-code contract — that is what made 0.21.0 a MINOR — and this cut
adds no verb, so the same reading makes this one a PATCH.

A CLOSED, UNSTAMPED ITEM IS STILL IN FLIGHT (.github#2225 — DEFECT class, and why this cut is OWED
rather than merely due). Closing is the MIDDLE of an item in this protocol, not its end: the merge
that closes the issue is followed by publication, receipts and registry records, and only then a
done stamp. Three read paths used `state = Closed` as a stand-in for "terminal" at the point where
facts are SELECTED, so the whole post-merge window went unread, and the one substitution failed in
three registers — `who` reported EMPTY for a live claim ("nothing in flight", not "cannot see");
`batch` reserved NOTHING, so a second worker could be dispatched into the holder's tree (.github#1858's
class); and `delivery` blamed the item's own `Paths:` line for the reader's blindness. `Scan.fs`'s
sweep is now gated on the done STAMP rather than on `Closed`; `Snapshot.fs`'s tolerance for an absent
body narrows to match across all four body-derived parsers, so a missing body on a closed, unstamped
row is a REFUSED document rather than an invented touch-set; and `who` gains arm C — closed board rows
that are not yet Done — which widens the READ and never the verdict, so a markerless closed row stays
silent rather than becoming UNCLAIMED. An overlapping candidate is refused with the byte-identical
sentence used for an open holder, naming the holder. Cost measured on the live 2119-row board: 2086
rows are closed and every one is stamped Done, so the extra reads are bounded by the number of workers
actually inside the post-merge window.

A QUOTED REVIEW MARKER IS INERT, NOT FATAL TO THE WHOLE PR (.github#2221). A comment that merely
QUOTES a review marker no longer invalidates every genuine marker on the pull request.

A MISPLACED MARKER IS REFUSED BY NAME, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED (.github#2221 round 1). A marker that is
prose-first, or carries one leading space, was dropped and the chain then reported as accepted. It is
now refused by name.

AND THE MISPLACEMENT RULE IS NOT VACUOUS FOR THE FIELD-LESS KINDS (.github#2221 round 2). Round 1's
discriminator required a protocol field key unconditionally, which made it vacuous for exactly the two
kinds that carry no field grammar — escalation and repair-phase — so seven of eight real prose-first
escalation shapes still vanished. Both kinds are now covered. Marker and field-read errors name the
offending comment id/URL, the field, and missing-versus-duplicated.

Every review chain this org parses until receivers restore 0.21.1 is parsed by the 0.21.0 engine that
.github#2221 was filed about, and every claim on a closed, unstamped row still reserves nothing.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.21.0):

0.21.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line: the typed semantic diff-audit becomes a
caller-visible engine command, and a mandatory, engine-recomputed gate on the live delivery path
(.github#2144).

FIFTEEN merged engine commits since 0.20.1 — fourteen from .github#2144 and its repair phase, plus
one DEFECT-class fix from .github#2220. The wire surface `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is
UNTOUCHED by this cut, so no exit code and no existing verb's contract changes.

BLOCKER-CLEARED NOW CHOOSES ITS REMEDY FROM THE ROW'S TOUCH-SET (.github#2220). The rule emitted
`Status = Ready` unconditionally, which is a correct answer to "do the recorded blockers still
hold?" applied to rows for which `Ready` is not a REACHABLE state. A row declaring `Paths: none`
(unschedulable by design) or declaring no touch-set line at all was advertised to every reader and
then refused by the scheduler on every pass — a permanently unfillable lane at the head of the
queue, observed live for six days on the board's only Critical row. Such rows now clear to
`Backlog`, the file-less chore case still clears to `Ready`, and an unreadable body yields no
destination rather than a guessed one. Receivers running 0.20.1 still reconcile the old way, which
is why this cut is owed rather than merely due.

NEW COMMAND VOCABULARY — `diff-audit`. `fsgg-coord-engine diff-audit <base> <head> <old> <new>
[receipt.json|-] [item-body.md] --paths P... [--repo ROOT] [--json]` inventories the exact
git-object changes between two immutable commits and classifies every changed occurrence with a
typed disposition. It is JSON-only, reads no board and opens no network connection, and accepts a
bare `-` to read a receipt from stdin. `--paths` is now accepted for it as well as for `widen` and
`set-paths`. THIS IS WHY THE CUT IS A MINOR AND NOT A PATCH: receivers gain a verb, a help entry, a
flag applicability, a render name and a refusal vocabulary that 0.20.1 did not have. The 0.x line
has no major available to take, so MINOR is this repository's caller-observable-change signal.

THE GATE. Review-chain parsing now binds a mandatory diff audit to an inventory the engine
recomputes ITSELF from the live PR base/head blobs, so a submitted receipt is evidence only where
the engine can reproduce it. Requiredness is derived from the live item body, the immutable head
declaration and an occurrence threshold — never from a review marker's own claim, and never from
caller environment variables. A receipt that is stale, incomplete, duplicated, malformed, or
outside the declared paths is refused, and unreadable live facts supply NO trusted facts and
require the audit rather than waiving it.

MEASURED IN OCCURRENCES, NOT FILES. Where no receipt supplies the rename tokens, the engine
recovers them from the live diff and counts OCCURRENCES. The changed-file count is a different and
always smaller quantity, and substituting it let a one-file/six-occurrence rename pass under the
default threshold of 5. Both arms — with and without a submitted receipt — now measure the same
way, from diff-aligned renames rather than from an unaligned whole-file multiset difference.

COVERAGE. A receipt carries one rename pair, and the gate is satisfied by the UNION of every
receipt the review chain carries: each must be honest about the pair it names, and together they
must cover every occurrence discovered across the whole diff. Before this, a receipt honestly
covering 6 of 12 discovered occurrences over 1 of 2 changed paths was accepted, so the author still
chose how much of the diff the audit applied to.

PERFORMANCE. Rename discovery buckets candidates by line skeleton, so a bulk rename over a large
diff terminates instead of degenerating into an all-pairs comparison.

Six refusal causes stay distinguishable rather than collapsing into one message: no receipts, a
malformed receipt, an honest-but-partial receipt, an unrecomputed rename pair, and a stale or
unresolved-disposition receipt each name themselves; only a covering union is `Ok`.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.20.1):

0.20.1 — PATCH: an organization board's row for an issue owned OUTSIDE the
board owner is now read from the board side, so cross-owner coordination reports the truth (#2204/#2209).

`Board.itemStatus` and `Board.itemBlockedBy` resolved a row's `Status`/`Blocked by` through the
issue-side `repository.issue.projectItems` connection, which does not surface an organization project's
row for an issue in a differently-owned repository. The narrowing found nothing and returned a DEFINITE
`Ok None` — "not on this board, or on it with no column" — manufactured out of a connection that had
merely filtered the row away. Both readers now route an external owner through one shared
`externalItemField`: the row is resolved by the cached item id and the field read as a one-point
`node(id:)` call, so the thrift that keeps `take` -> `claim` off a full-board scan is preserved, and the
board owner's own issues keep the existing issue-side read unchanged. An unresolvable lookup is now
`Error`; `Ok None` means measured absence only.

Three caller-visible behaviors are repaired for cross-owner rows, each pinned by a fixture reproducing
the pre-fix symptom: `claim`/`take --json` can report `converged: true` (it was permanently false);
bare `release` restores the pre-claim column instead of stranding the row at `In progress`; and `add` no
longer lays the `Backlog` default over a live external column.

Patch is correct: no verb, flag, result or exit-code vocabulary is added or removed, and the wire
surface `src/FS.GG.Coord.Core/Protocol.fs` is untouched by this cut. This is a compatibility-preserving
correctness fix to 0.20.0's behavior.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.20.0):

0.20.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line: deterministic, resumable coordination cycles
are now a caller-visible engine command (#2133/#2197).

The new `cycle` surface inspects, registers, advances, updates, and completes source-bound roadmap and
workspace units through one typed ledger. Stable provider-cycle identities bind implementation, critique,
feedback, candidate head, merge evidence, and durable update history; stale or wrong-cycle artifacts fail
closed. The default journal resolves through Git's per-worktree path, so restart/resume works in the linked
worktrees used by normal workers.

Provider validation executes only the canonical validators shipped beside the engine, with pinned byte
identities. Caller-controlled artifact roots cannot substitute executable validators, tampered bundled
validators are refused, and the SDD provider is bound to the supported 1.0.0 tool/report/work identity.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.19.1):

0.19.1 — PATCH: coherent Blocked parking is now enforced consistently across every board-writing
transport route (#2109/#2184).

The packaged coordination engine rejects an incoherent `Status: Blocked` write before it can leave a
board row parked without a concrete blocker or the explicit human/action sentinel. The centralized
coverage inventory includes add, release, reconcile, and restored-status writers, so future transport
routes cannot silently bypass the same guard. This is a compatibility-preserving correctness patch to
0.19.0's caller-visible lifecycle contract.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.18.0):

Runtime changes merged after 0.17.0 make the packaged engine match the coordination and product-board
guidance already carried by Kit 0.24.0 and the driver manifest.

REPOSITORY-SCOPED TOUCH SETS (#2011): path declarations are interpreted in their declared Repo Scope,
so identical relative paths in different repositories no longer contend accidentally.

BOARD FACTS AND DIAGNOSTICS (#2040/#2042): scheduler facts are extracted behind a typed application
boundary, overlap refusals name the reserving holder, and board drivers receive structured rate-limit
classes instead of parsing prose (#2041).
